articles.body:
49ers vs Rams: NFL kicks off 2026 season with historic showdown in Australia

The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams will make NFL history when they open the 2026 regular season at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in Australia, marking the league's first-ever regular-season game on Australian soil . More than 100,000 fans are expected to fill the iconic stadium for one of the most anticipated Week 1 matchups.

Beyond the historic venue, one of the biggest storylines is how each team prepared for the longest road trip in NFL history . The 49ers traveled to Australia more than a week before kickoff to adjust to the 16-hour time difference, while Sean McVay and the Rams chose to remain in California until less than 30 hours before the game, hoping to minimize the effects of jet lag.

San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed the contrasting travel strategies, insisting the outcome will come down to execution rather than preparation.

The game also features two of the top Super Bowl contenders in the NFC. The Rams strengthened their defense by adding Myles Garrett , Trent McDuffie , and Jaylen Watson , although Aaron Donald will not travel to Australia as he continues ramping up following his return from retirement.

The 49ers , meanwhile, expect key stars Nick Bosa and George Kittle to return after injury, giving quarterback Brock Purdy one of the NFL's most talented supporting casts alongside Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams .

One of the key battles to watch will be Myles Garrett and Byron Young against the 49ers' offensive tackles, Trent Williams and Colton McKivitz . Garrett's debut in a Rams uniform could play a decisive role in determining the outcome of the historic opener.

49ers vs Rams: Date, time and how to watch

Game: San Francisco 49ers vs. Los Angeles Rams

Venue: Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), Melbourne, Australia

Betting odds: Rams (-3.5)

With Week 1 set to begin on the other side of the world, the 49ers vs. Rams showdown promises to deliver playoff intensity, Super Bowl expectations, and a historic moment for the NFL as it expands its global footprint.

The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams are about to make NFL history, traveling halfway across the globe to open the 2026 season in Melbourne, Australia , where more than 100,000 fans are expected to pack the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground for the league's first-ever regular-season game on Australian soil.

While the historic setting has grabbed headlines, so has the vastly different approach each team has taken to preparing for the longest road trip in NFL history.

The 49ers arrived in Australia more than a week before kickoff, giving players time to acclimate to the 16-hour time difference while embracing the opportunity to connect with local fans ahead of the landmark event.

The Rams, meanwhile, opted for the opposite strategy. Sean McVay's team is scheduled to land in Melbourne less than 30 hours before kickoff, believing the best way to combat jet lag is to remain on California time for as long as possible.

Despite the contrasting philosophies, neither team believes the outcome will validate one approach over the other.

"I'm sure people will study it afterward and try to decide which method worked," 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "But football games are won by the team that plays better, not by who got on the plane first."

Instead, the focus remains on what promises to be one of the marquee matchups of Week 1.

The Rams enter the season as one of the favorites to win the Super Bowl after assembling perhaps the NFL's most talented roster, while the 49ers believe a healthier lineup can return them to championship contention after injuries derailed parts of their 2025 campaign.

The rivalry has become one of the NFL's fiercest over the past decade, with Shanahan and McVay consistently pushing each other in the NFC West. Now, they meet on an international stage unlike anything either franchise has experienced.

"It's a unique challenge," said new Rams star Myles Garrett . "Both organizations have their own plan to deal with the travel and the time difference. At the end of the day, we'll find out on the field whose preparation paid off."

Garrett headlines a revamped Los Angeles defense alongside newcomers Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson , but one notable name won't be making the trip.

Despite ending his retirement last month, Aaron Donald will remain in Los Angeles as he continues working his way back into football shape. The Rams chose not to rush the 35-year-old defensive legend, preserving him for later in the season.

Shanahan admitted he fully expected Donald to suit up in Australia.

"I've never been happier to be wrong," the 49ers coach joked.

San Francisco, meanwhile, expects Nick Bosa and George Kittle to return after lengthy injury recoveries, although Shanahan has yet to determine how many snaps either star will play.

Matchup: San Francisco 49ers (13-6) vs. Los Angeles Rams (14-6)

Kickoff: Thursday, 8:35 p.m. ET

Last meeting: Rams 42, 49ers 26 (Nov. 9, 2025)

All-time series: 49ers lead 78-71-3

Myles Garrett and Byron Young vs. Trent Williams and Colton McKivitz

All eyes will be on the line of scrimmage.

Garrett makes his highly anticipated Rams debut, forming a dangerous pass-rushing tandem with Byron Young . Their first assignment couldn't be much tougher: protecting Brock Purdy behind future Hall of Fame left tackle Trent Williams and right tackle Colton McKivitz .

Garrett has the ability to change a game with one play, but Shanahan's offense has historically limited Los Angeles' pass rush. In two meetings last season, the Rams managed just one sack despite facing backup quarterback Mac Jones for much of the year. Whether that trend continues could go a long way toward deciding the NFL's first game in Australia.
